facts.text: Semantic or object-list replay uses real decision, warning and braking logic downstream of perception.
facts.quote: **What is real:** the decision, warning and braking logic downstream of perception.

facts.text: Semantic or object-list replay requires ground-truth or pre-recorded object lists in common coordinates, plus machine state.
facts.quote: **Needs:** ground-truth or pre-recorded object lists in common coordinates, plus machine state.

facts.text: Semantic or object-list replay can run open-loop or closed-loop.
facts.quote: Can be run open-loop or closed-loop.

facts.text: Semantic or object-list replay proves decision thresholds, warning logic, threat assessment and brake-request logic independently of sensor modality.
facts.quote: **Proves:** decision thresholds, warning logic, threat assessment and brake-request logic independent of sensor modality.

facts.text: Semantic or object-list replay is the cheapest way to sweep large scenario sets.
facts.quote: It is the cheapest way to sweep large scenario sets.

facts.text: Semantic or object-list replay cannot prove perception.
Semantic or object-list replay can hide sensor latency, occlusion, false detections and range or classification errors because it assumes perception has already succeeded.
facts.quote: It can hide sensor latency, occlusion, false detections and range or classification errors, because it assumes perception has already succeeded.
